text:
amira: quick sync after the striping spike. are we comfortable defaulting to a regional singleton gateway for most tenants, and making per-AZ striping opt-in for high-throughput / low-tail-latency customers?

max: leaning singleton by default. simpler routing and way fewer ENIs and route entries. cost and ops overhead win here.

sasha: +1 for default singleton, but we need answers on cert rotation and control-plane connection scale if we later opt many connectors for a tenant. propose a cert-manager controller and a multiplexed control tunnel.

rachel: also watch route table limits for customers using route-based connectivity. striping will blow up route counts quickly. add an infra CI warning if projected routes > threshold.

infra-bot: spike artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-spikes/connector-striping/results-2026-03-15.tgz

amira: migration mechanics: DNS-based canary (tenant connector CNAME, low TTL) seems safest. roll 1% -> 10% -> 100% with healthchecks (p95, 5xx, snat_port_usage). immediate rollback via DNS revert.

max: agree. also include a gradual ENI attach guard to avoid route propagation spikes.

sasha: operator playbook items: emergency cert rotation steps, SNAT pool refill script, and metrics to monitor during cutover. I'll draft it.

rachel: i'll add CI checks for route counts and an attach-rate limiter in infra pipelines.

amira: decision draft: default = singleton regional gateway for tenants under threshold T (cost and simplicity). high-throughput or latency-sensitive tenants may opt into per-AZ striping. action items: sasha -> playbook; max -> DNS canary automation; rachel -> infra checks; amira -> RFC addendum.

max: tiny appendix idea: include PrivateLink option for customers that can't accept extra routes; higher cost but avoids route growth.

amira: include PrivateLink as appendix. thanks all, i'll write the addendum today. :rocket:
